questions.question: What is a Pull Request (PR) on GitHub?

options.A: A request asking GitHub for more storage space
options.B: A proposed set of code changes from a branch submitted for review and discussion before merging into a target branch
options.C: A command that downloads code from the terminal

questions.explanation: A PR allows team members to review code, run automated tests, discuss implementation details, and approve changes before merging.

questions.question: In a GitHub Pull Request, what is the 'base' branch?

options.A: The branch where you made your changes
options.B: The target destination branch that will RECEIVE the merged changes (e.g. `main`)

questions.explanation: Base is where you want to merge your changes INTO. Head/Compare is the branch containing your new commits.

questions.question: Where on a GitHub PR can reviewers see the exact line-by-line diff of all modified files?
questions.explanation: The 'Files changed' tab displays side-by-side or unified diffs for every file modified in the pull request.

questions.question: If a reviewer asks for changes on your PR, how do you update the Pull Request?

options.A: Close the PR and open a brand new one
options.B: Make the requested edits locally, commit them on the same feature branch, and run `git push` — the PR updates automatically!
options.C: Email the updated file to the reviewer

questions.explanation: GitHub PRs track the branch. Any new commits pushed to that branch automatically appear in the open PR.

questions.question: What is a 'Draft Pull Request' on GitHub?

options.A: A PR that cannot be opened
options.B: A PR marked as work-in-progress that cannot be merged until marked ready for review
options.D: A PR that expires after 1 hour

questions.explanation: Draft PRs let developers get early feedback or run CI tests without accidentally allowing the code to be merged.

questions.question: What are the three standard merge options available when merging a PR on GitHub?

options.B: Create a merge commit, Squash and merge, Rebase and merge

questions.explanation: GitHub offers: regular merge commit (keeps all commits), squash and merge (combines all commits into one clean commit), and rebase (linear history).

questions.question: What does 'Squash and Merge' do to a PR with 15 small commits?

options.A: Deletes all 15 commits and cancels the merge
options.B: Combines all 15 commits into a single unified commit on the base branch with a clean message

questions.explanation: Squash and merge condenses messy work-in-progress commits into one polished commit on `main`.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered constructive code review etiquette?

options.B: Explaining the reasoning behind suggestions, being respectful, and praising good solutions

questions.explanation: Code review is a collaborative learning culture. Professional reviews focus on code quality and explain *why* an alternative is better.

questions.question: How can a reviewer suggest an exact code replacement directly in an inline GitHub comment?

options.A: Using the 'Add a suggestion' button (```suggestion block)
options.B: By editing the author's local file
options.C: By calling the author on the phone

questions.explanation: GitHub allows reviewers to insert ```` ```suggestion ```` blocks, which the PR author can apply with a single click.

questions.question: After merging a Pull Request on GitHub, what is the best practice for the local repository?

options.B: Switch to local `main`, run `git pull origin main` to download the merged changes, and delete the local feature branch
options.C: Re-clone the entire repository from scratch

questions.explanation: Syncing your local `main` with `git pull` brings your computer up to date with the newly merged PR code.
